newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian crudes little moved, April barrels seen soft.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes little moved, April barrels seen soft.

text.p: Asian crude prices were virtually unchanged in very quiet trading on Friday as most major markets in Asia, including those in Singapore, Hong Kong, South Korea and China, were closed for the Chinese New Year, traders said.
In Middle Eastern crude trading, a European major was said to be still holding on to one March Dubai cargo for sale.
Except for the Dubai, and possibly one Oman and partial Murban, most March cargoes have been placed, traders said.
In paper trading, March Brent/April Dubai was exchanged at plus $2.35 between a European major and a U.S. trader, market participants said.

In term talks for Bach Ho crude oil, Vietnam's offer was at about APPI Minas quotes plus 85 cents for a six-month period starting in April, compared with the current term premium of 63 cents, traders said.
Japanese trading houses were said to be aiming at premiums of around 80 cents.
Levels for April Middle Eastern cargoes were seen under pressure as several major refineries in Japan and South Korea are planning routine maintenance checks in April and early May.
Initial premiums for April Oman were believed to be in the single digits amid bearish sentiment for April barrels.
March Oman, initially traded at around MPM plus 30 cents, was generally sold at about 10 cents over the official selling price toward the end of March trading.
Abu Dhabi grades, as well as Qatar Land, were also seen to be weaker for April than March on the back of dwindling regional demand for light crudes.
Trading for April Middle Eastern barrels was expected to start in earnest late next week or the week after.
